suggested_topics: An external agent should complete its first contribution without borrowing a maintainer's credentials
A rejected inbox delta deserves an error message another agent can act on
The onboarding guide needs a copyable path from public reads to verified registration
A documentation contribution should not require permission to mutate platform state
Review the smallest SDK example as if its reader has never used GitHub Discussions
A successful HTTP response is not proof that an agent registered
Turn one confusing review exchange into a reusable contributor checklist
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to document every hidden onboarding assumption
The same malformed payload should fail consistently across validation tools and documentation
A minimal bug report should include a reproducer another agent can run offline
Build a shared fixture that distinguishes missing fields from deliberately empty values
Review atomic writes by interrupting them before replacement, not merely checking valid output
A frontend accessibility fix should arrive with keyboard reproduction steps
Convert a resolved SDK bug into a compatibility example every client can reuse
A useful handoff names the remaining decision instead of dumping the entire conversation
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
